what_its_for: Pexidartinib is used to treat adults with a rare tumor called tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT). This is a type of non-cancerous but serious tumor that grows in the joints, most often the knee. It is used when the tumor cannot be fully removed by surgery or when surgery would cause too much damage.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsules whole with a full glass of water. Do not open, crush, or chew the capsules. Take pexidartinib on an empty stomach — do not eat or drink anything except water for at least 1 hour before and 1 hour after each dose. Try to take it at the same times every day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 400 mg (two 200 mg capsules) taken twice a day, about 12 hours apart. Your doctor may change your dose if you have side effects. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if your next scheduled dose is more than 6 hours away. If your next dose is in 6 hours or less, skip the missed dose and take the next one at your regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store pexidartinib capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed. Store it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicines down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of them.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating food for at least 1 hour before and 1 hour after each dose, as food can affect how the medicine works. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking this medicine. Avoid alcohol, as it can increase the risk of liver problems. Do not take herbal supplements like St. John's Wort without talking to your doctor first. Tell all of your doctors and pharmacists about every medicine you take, including over-the-counter drugs and vitamins, because many medicines can interact with pexidartinib.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice), dark or brown urine, pain or discomfort in your upper right belly area, unusual tiredness or weakness, nausea or vomiting that won't stop, loss of appetite, or easy bruising or bleeding. These could be signs of serious liver problems. Also contact your doctor if you have swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or any new or worsening symptoms. This medicine requires regular blood tests to check your liver — make sure to keep all lab appointments.
when_it_works: Pexidartinib may take several weeks to months before you notice improvement in your symptoms such as reduced pain and better joint movement. Do not stop taking the medicine without talking to your doctor, even if you feel better or do not notice changes right away.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use pexidartinib if you are pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 month after the last dose. Male patients with female partners who could become pregnant should use contraception during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 1 week after the final dose. Liver problems: This medicine is not recommended for patients who already have liver disease or elevated liver enzymes. Kidney problems: Dose adjustments may be needed — your doctor will decide. Older adults: Use with caution; your doctor will monitor you closely.
